stem:
Sia wants a quicker way to compute $24 \times 25$.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: Replace $25$ with $\dfrac{100}{4}$, divide $24$ by $4$, then multiply by $100$ to get $600$.
The shortcut fits here because $25$ has a simple relationship to $100$.
The same power-of-ten rewrite works for every factor, even when it has no simple link to $10$, $100$, or $1000$.
Start from $600$ and reverse to invent both factors $24$ and $25$.

teacher.key_rationale: 25=100/4, so 24×25=(24/4)×100=600. The method needs a simple link to a power of ten. Extending it to arbitrary factors drops that condition. Working backwards from 600 reverses the calculation.
